chunks: Al-Kafi: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Ibn Riab and from more than one, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Whoever worships Allah by imagining Him (in his mind) then he has disbelieved. And whoever worships the Name without the Meaning (the reality behind the name) then he has disbelieved. And whoever worships both the Name and the Meaning then he has associated partners with Him. And whoever worships the Meaning while applying the Names to Him with the attributes by which He described Himself, fixing his heart upon that and expressing it with his tongue in his secrets and his public life, then those are the true companions of the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him). And in another report: those are the true believers.

key_terms.الْمَعْنَى: The Meaning or Essence behind the name

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between worshipping the Name of God and worshipping His Meaning in Shia theology?
ai.summary: This hadith delineates the epistemological hierarchy of Tawhid, moving from superficial 'worship by conjecture' (Al-Tawhum) to the profound realization of the Divine Essence through the precise application of His self-described attributes. It identifies the true adherents of Imam Ali (AS) as those who maintain a balanced worship of both the Name and the Meaning, avoiding the extremes of literalism and abstract associationism. This framework underscores the Shia emphasis on deep theological understanding (Ma'rifah) as the hallmark of genuine faith.
